idiom_name: persistent classes with a hand-written join mapper (libpqxx / SOCI / Qt SQL)
implementation_notes: C++ has the class hierarchy the pattern assumes, but the standard library has no ORM: declare the classes, map each class to its table and write the join per load (or let the mapper issue a second query for subclass columns), using whichever SQL client is already in the stack. What replaces the classic structure is a mapper type per hierarchy node that owns the SQL text and the row-to-object conversion, with a virtual destructor and a type-code switch for polymorphic load; a code-generating ORM (ODB) removes boilerplate but the joined layout and key foreign keys stay a manual decision. Hand-written mapping is justified when the schema is shared with other applications or when only a couple of paths are ever read.
pitfalls: Polymorphic deletion needs a virtual destructor on the base class, or deleting through a base pointer frees only the base part and leaks the derived members.
Nothing enforces the join: a mapper that forgets one table of the path still compiles and returns a half-filled object, so write one loader per class and keep it the only place that touches SQL.
